note:
Researched from live web sources in a Claude Code session — no paid API, no key, no cost.

`case` is the argument for picking them; `watch_out` is the honest counter-argument, because a recommendation you can't argue against isn't advice. `key_stats` holds the hard numbers as discrete facts so they can be shown next to any decision the app makes. `voices` records what named outlets actually said — 'analysts say' is not a source. `dissent` marks a genuine split, which damps the player's weighting rather than presenting a contested pick as settled.

This is the first gameweek researched against real results rather than pre-season expectation. The dominant theme in the coverage is kneejerk risk: Haaland blanked, Manchester United flopped, Tottenham were beaten heavily and Hull City won, and almost every outlet is warning against acting on one weekend. The entries below are weighted accordingly — a GW1 haul on its own is treated as thin evidence unless something structural sits behind it.

Club-wide verdicts do NOT belong here; they live in teams.json.

players.name: De Cuyper
players.verdict: The most-bought player in the game, and for once the bandwagon has a structural reason behind it.
players.case: He was the highest-scoring player of Gameweek 1 on 17 points — four shots, three key passes, a goal and an assist — and his 1.68 expected goal involvements was the highest of any player in the round, not just any Brighton player. The reason that isn't simply a one-week spike is positional: he played as a left winger rather than a full-back, and with Minteh expected to be out for around two months there is a good chance he keeps the advanced role. That gives him a midfielder's attacking upside while FPL still classifies him as a defender, which is the single most valuable mispricing available in this game.
players.watch_out: The whole case rests on a role that has been seen once. If Minteh returns early, or Brighton revert him to left-back, what remains is a full-back at an inflated price with none of the upside being paid for. Nearly 250,000 managers have already bought him, so the differential value is gone too — you are buying at the top of the bandwagon.
key_stats: 17 points in GW1 — the highest score of any player
1.68 xGI in GW1 — the highest of any player in the round
4 shots and 3 key passes from a defender-classified player
Played left wing, not left-back; Minteh out roughly two months
~250,000 transfers in ahead of GW2 — the most-bought player in the game

voices.take: Call him a perfectly reasonable transfer if you didn't start with him, and single out the positional change rather than the 17 points as the real reason.
Ran a dedicated buy-keep-or-sell piece on him ahead of GW2, which is itself a signal of how much of the community is weighing this move.

players.name: Calafiori
players.verdict: Delivered exactly what the pre-season case said he would, and the fixtures haven't turned yet.
players.case: He continued his Community Shield form into the opening weekend with an assist and a clean sheet, which is the specific combination that makes an attacking defender worth owning — the floor and the ceiling arriving in the same afternoon. He is one of three Arsenal players among the eight most-bought ahead of GW2, alongside Odegaard and Tzolis, so the market has moved to the same conclusion. Arsenal's opening run remains the softest in the league.
players.watch_out: Arsenal's defensive rotation is still unsettled with first-choice centre-backs working back to fitness, and Calafiori is the one whose place is least assured when everyone is available. He was a differential a week ago and isn't now, so you are paying a higher price for a place in the side that is no more certain than it was.
key_stats: Assist and a clean sheet in GW1
One of three Arsenal players in the eight most-bought ahead of GW2
Carried Community Shield form straight into the league season

voices.take: Group him with Odegaard and Tzolis as the Arsenal players the market moved to after the opening weekend.
Note he is receiving attention specifically for continuing his Community Shield form rather than for a single result.

players.name: Haaland
players.verdict: Blanked in GW1 and is still not a player to sell — but the must-have framing has to go.
players.case: The underlying case has not changed: he led the league last season in shots per game, big chances per game and expected goals per game simultaneously, and has finished as the top-scoring player after six gameweeks in all four of his Manchester City seasons. One blank against that pattern is noise. City travel to Crystal Palace in GW2.
players.watch_out: He blanked in the opening round and costs £15.5m, so the opportunity cost of holding is real and immediate. At around 71% ownership he is also not a route to rank — see the dissent below, which is now the more interesting half of this entry.
key_stats: Blanked in GW1
£15.5m — around a sixth of the total budget
~71% owned
Led the league in shots, big chances and xG per game last season
GW2: Crystal Palace away

voices.take: Led their Gameweek 1 review with the blank, alongside Manchester United flopping and Hull City winning, as the results that most upset the template.
Warn explicitly against kneejerk transfers after the opening weekend and to judge on underlying numbers rather than one scoreline.

dissent.case: At roughly 71% ownership his haul barely moves your rank and his blank barely hurts it — owning and captaining him is tracking the field rather than beating it. After a blanking opening weekend a meaningful minority are arguing the £15.5m is better spread across two players with better GW2 fixtures. That is a real argument about rank rather than about whether he is good.

players.name: B.Fernandes
players.verdict: Among the most-sold in the game after a poor opening weekend — into the best fixture on the board.
players.case: Manchester United host Ipswich in GW2, which alongside their GW1 trip to Hull was the best back-to-back opening any side was handed. He remains on penalties, corners and direct free-kicks, and last season produced 9 goals and a record 24 assists. The case for holding is that the fixture people bought him for has not been played yet.
players.watch_out: United flopped in GW1 and he is among the most-sold players in the game as a result, so this is a hold that will feel worse before it feels better. The pre-season penalty misses that Fantasy Football Scout flagged remain unresolved, and his case leans on dead balls more than most.
key_stats: 9 goals and 24 assists last season — a record FPL assist total
On penalties, corners and direct free-kicks
Among the most-sold players ahead of GW2
GW2: Ipswich at home, after Hull away in GW1

voices.take: List him among the most-sold players ahead of Gameweek 2, following Manchester United's poor opening result.
Frame selling him now as the archetypal kneejerk — moving off a premium one week before the fixture he was bought for.

players.name: Sangare
players.verdict: The week's second bandwagon, off a haul against Spurs.
players.case: He hauled in the opening weekend against a Tottenham side that was comprehensively beaten, and has attracted almost 200,000 new owners as a result. At his price he is the kind of budget enabler that makes a premium-heavy structure affordable, which is the job most managers are actually trying to fill this week.
players.watch_out: One haul against a team having a bad day is the thinnest evidence in this file. Nothing about the underlying numbers has been established, and the entire ownership move is built on a single afternoon — the exact pattern AllAboutFPL are warning against this week.
key_stats: Hauled against Tottenham in GW1
~200,000 transfers in ahead of GW2
One of the two biggest bandwagons of the week

voices.take: Name him alongside De Cuyper as the early bandwagon of the week, having attracted almost 200,000 new owners.
Caution that a transfer should be for a player who stays in the team for several gameweeks, not one bought purely on a GW1 result.

players.name: Palmer
players.verdict: Right player, wrong week — Chelsea meet the defence that gave up nothing in GW1.
players.case: Chelsea were excellent against Fulham on the opening weekend and he is the focal point of that attack.
players.watch_out: Brighton are the opponent, and they are a different proposition to Fulham: among the best defences in the league last season, and they allowed their GW1 opponents zero shots on target. Analysts are explicitly saying to think twice about buying Chelsea attackers into this fixture. Buying an attacker for one week against a defence in that form is paying full price for the worst version of him.
key_stats: Chelsea beat Fulham convincingly in GW1
Brighton allowed zero shots on target in GW1
Brighton were among the best defences in the league last season

voices.take: Say managers should think twice about bringing in Chelsea's attackers this week specifically because Brighton are a different proposition to Fulham.
Advise buying players who hold their place for several gameweeks rather than chasing a single favourable-looking fixture.

players.name: Joao Pedro
players.verdict: Same fixture problem as Palmer, and he is far more widely owned.
players.case: He led the line in a Chelsea side that opened the season by taking Fulham apart, and arrived fresher than almost anyone after missing the World Cup.
players.watch_out: Brighton in GW2 is the issue: zero shots on target conceded in the opening weekend and one of the meanest defensive records in the league last season. At around 44% ownership the downside is shared with much of the field, which softens the rank damage but does nothing for your actual score. This is a hold-and-wait rather than a buy.
key_stats: ~44% owned
Chelsea beat Fulham convincingly in GW1
Brighton conceded zero shots on target in GW1
7 goals in 6 pre-season appearances

voices.take: Name him directly among the Chelsea attackers to think twice about this week, because of the Brighton fixture rather than his form.
Had him on the official must-have list pre-season, which is why the ownership is high enough for this fixture to matter to so many teams.

players.name: Porro
players.verdict: A fitness doubt in a side that was taken apart in GW1.
players.case: An attacking full-back with genuine set-piece involvement when fit and starting.
players.watch_out: He is being eased back for match fitness and was named on the bench in a cup tie, so the minutes are not there yet. He is among the most-sold players in the game after the opening weekend, and Tottenham were comprehensively beaten. A defender you are not sure will start, in a defence that just shipped a bad result, is the easiest sell in this file.

players.watch_out: He is reported as injured again with a shoulder issue and not ready to feature. There is nothing to weigh until he is fit.
